# Behavioral Design Specification: KMAC Application Interface

## 1. Overview

This module is the control and data-routing front end for the KMAC/SHA3 engine. It selects between two operation classes:

- **Software-initiated operations**, in which a software command stream controls the hash/KMAC process.
- **Application-initiated operations**, in which one of several application interfaces starts a message transfer and later receives the resulting digest.

The module does not perform Keccak computation, padding, or KMAC keyed processing itself. It is responsible for:

- Arbitrating ownership of the KMAC/SHA3 engine.
- Selecting the active configuration source.
- Selecting the secret-key source.
- Routing message data into the downstream message FIFO.
- Routing Keccak state or digest data to the correct consumer.
- Reporting locally detected misuse errors.

---

## 2. Operation Ownership and Arbitration

The module shall be in an idle state after reset. In idle, it may grant ownership of the engine to one of two kinds of requesters:

1. An application interface that presents a first message beat while the sideloaded key is valid.
2. A software start command.

The following rules shall apply:

- If an application request and a software start request arrive at the same time, the application request shall take precedence, provided the sideloaded key is valid.
- If more than one application interface presents a request at the same time, the module shall select one according to a fixed priority. Only one application interface may become active at a time.
- Once an application interface is granted ownership, that interface shall remain the active source until its operation completes. All other application requests are ignored during that time.
- Once software is granted ownership, all application requests are ignored until software explicitly ends the operation.
- Application requests that are not granted are not acknowledged and may be retried later.

---

## 3. Software-Initiated Operation

A software operation begins when the module is idle and software issues a start command.

While software owns the operation, the module shall:

- Forward software command words to the KMAC/SHA3 engine.
- Accept software message data and forward it to the message FIFO.
- Honor downstream FIFO backpressure. A software data beat shall only be accepted when the message FIFO is able to accept it.
- Forward the software-supplied data mask unchanged.
- Forward the absorption-complete indication from the downstream engine to software.
- Make the Keccak state and state-valid indication visible to the software state window.

Software shall be responsible for including any required KMAC output-length encoding in its own message stream. The module must not automatically append an encoded output length during software operations.

For software operations:

- The secret key shall come from the software-configured key, unless the sideload-key enable is set.
- If the sideload-key enable is set, the secret key shall come from the sideloaded key.
- The key length, SHA3 mode, KMAC enable, Keccak strength, and prefix shall come from the software register configuration.

The software operation ends when software issues the done command. At that point, the module shall return to idle, release ownership, and restore the software register configuration as the default configuration.

---

## 4. Application-Initiated Operation

An application operation begins when an application interface presents a first data beat while the module is idle and the sideloaded key is valid. The first data beat therefore acts as both the start request and the first message beat.

While an application operation is active:

- The selected application interface shall be the only source of application message data.
- The module shall apply the configuration associated with that application interface rather than the software register configuration.
- The module shall ignore software data writes. A software data write during an application operation shall be treated as an error and shall not enter the message FIFO.
- The module shall ignore software commands that do not apply to application operations. A software command other than a no-operation or start command during an application operation shall be treated as an error.

### 4.1 Application Message Data

For the selected application interface, the module shall:

- Accept data beats only when the downstream message FIFO can accept them.
- Forward the application data to the message FIFO in the same width as the FIFO interface.
- Convert the application byte-enable strobes into the corresponding byte mask. A byte with its strobe asserted shall be written; a byte without its strobe asserted shall be masked off.
- Allow partial words. The application is not required to present all byte lanes in every beat.

When the final beat of the application message is accepted, the module shall start the completion sequence for that application.

### 4.2 End-of-Message Handling

If the application operation is a KMAC operation, the module shall append one encoded-output-length word to the message FIFO before issuing the process command. The encoded value shall correspond to the application digest width. The module shall wait until this word is accepted by the message FIFO.

If the application operation is a SHA3 operation, no output-length word shall be appended.

After all required end-of-message data has been written, the module shall send a process command to the downstream engine.

### 4.3 Application Completion

When the downstream engine indicates that absorption is complete, the module shall:

- Present the digest to the selected application interface.
- Assert the application done indication.
- Send the done command downstream.
- Clear the application selection and return to idle.

The module shall not expose the Keccak state to the software state window during an application operation. The state window shall be inactive and its data outputs shall be zero.

---

## 5. Secret-Key Selection

The module shall select the secret key based on the active operation and configuration.

### 5.1 Software-Initiated Operations

- By default, the secret key shall be taken from the software-provided key shares.
- The key length shall be taken from the software key-length configuration.
- If the sideload-key enable is set, the secret key shall be taken from the sideloaded key instead.
- When the sideloaded key is used in a software operation, the key length shall be derived from the expected application digest width rather than from the software key-length register.

### 5.2 Application-Initiated Operations

- For an application KMAC operation, the secret key shall always be taken from the sideloaded key, independent of the software sideload-key enable.
- For an application KMAC operation, the key length shall match the expected application digest width.

### 5.3 Key Form

The sideloaded key is always supplied in two shares.

- If masking is enabled, the module shall preserve the two-share form and deliver both shares to the KMAC core.
- If masking is disabled, the module shall combine the two sideloaded shares into a single unmasked key before delivery.

The software-provided key shall pass through in the form provided by the configuration.

---

## 6. Configuration Selection

### 6.1 Software Operations

During software-owned operations, the module shall use the software register configuration for:

- SHA3 mode.
- Keccak strength.
- KMAC enable.
- Prefix.

### 6.2 Application Operations

During an application operation, the module shall use the selected application’s configuration rather than the software register configuration.

- If the application is configured for SHA3 mode, the module shall present plain SHA3 mode and disable KMAC.
- If the application is configured for KMAC mode, the module shall present cSHAKE mode and enable KMAC.
- The Keccak strength shall be taken from the application configuration.

### 6.3 Prefix Selection

For software operations, the software-configured prefix shall always be used.

For an application operation, the prefix source shall be selected by the application configuration:

- When the application prefix mode is disabled, the software-configured prefix shall be used.
- When the application prefix mode is enabled, the application-specific prefix shall be used.

When an application operation completes, the module shall restore the software configuration as the active default so that the next software operation starts from the expected register state.

---

## 7. Keccak State and Digest Delivery

### 7.1 Software State Access

While software owns the operation, the module shall forward the Keccak state and its state-valid indication to the software state window.

When the module is not in a software-owned operation, the software state window shall receive:

- No state-valid assertion.
- Zero data on all state outputs.

This prevents the Keccak state from being visible to software while an application operation is in progress.

### 7.2 Application Digest Delivery

When an application operation completes absorption, the module shall deliver the digest to the selected application interface only.

The digest shall be the portion of the Keccak state corresponding to the expected application digest width.

- If masking is enabled, the digest shall be delivered in two shares.
- If masking is disabled, the digest shall be delivered as one share and the second share shall be zero.

Non-selected application interfaces shall receive no digest, no done indication, and no error indication.

---

## 8. Error Behavior

The module shall detect and report the following local error conditions:

- Software presents message data when software is not the active owner of the engine.
- Software presents a command other than a no-operation or start command while an application operation is active.
- An application KMAC operation is selected or is starting, but the sideloaded key is not valid.

The module shall output a valid error report for the cycle in which one of these conditions is detected.

If the key-not-valid condition occurs, the module shall not proceed with the application operation. It shall remain in an error state and shall not accept new software or application operations until the next reset.

The module shall also propagate an external error indication from the downstream hash engine to the active application interface. If no application interface is active, the downstream error indication shall not be presented on any application response.

---

## 9. Reset Behavior

On reset, the module shall:

- Return to idle.
- Release all ownership and application selection.
- Select the software register configuration as the default.
- Deassert all active operation commands.
- Present no digest, no done, no state-valid indication.
- Drive the software state window to zero.
- Report no error.
